paper_metadata.title: High temperature strength at 1773 K and room temperature fracture toughness of Nbss/Nb5Si3 in situ composites alloyed with Mo

alloy_systems.name: Nb-Si-Mo in situ composite

evidence.quote: High temperature compressive strength at 1773 K and room temperature fracture toughness have been studied in terms of microstructure, phase stability and solid solution hardening in Nb-Si-Mo in situ composites consisting of niobium solid solution and Nb5Si3.

property_observations.material_state: arc-melted and heat treated at 1973 K for 48 h

evidence.quote: Yield stresses increased with increasing volume fraction of Nb5Si3 but exhibited a sudden decrease at 52% of Nb5Si3 phase and then increased again with further increasing volume fraction of Nb5Si3 in the alloys heat treated at 1973 K.
It is found that molybdenum has a strong effect to increase the yield stress of the present in situ composite at 1773 K due to solid solution hardening.

mechanisms.name: plastic deformation of Nb solid solution

evidence.quote: It is suggested that plastic deformation of Nb solid solution and interface decohesion is responsible for high fracture toughness in this alloy system.
